question: What is the purpose of the hazardous materials "containment rules"?
choice_a: To tell shippers how to package materials safely and drivers how to load, transport, and unload them
choice_b: To set uniform freight rates for hazardous cargo
choice_c: To require every carrier to hire a chemist
choice_d: To eliminate the need for shipping papers
explanation: The manual states the regulations 'tell shippers how to package the materials safely and drivers how to load, transport, and unload the material. These are called "containment rules."'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: How do shippers communicate the risk of a hazardous material to carriers and drivers?
choice_a: By calling the driver's dispatcher before every trip
choice_b: By putting hazard warning labels on packages and providing shipping papers, emergency response information, and placards
choice_c: By posting warnings on the shipper's website
choice_d: By painting the cargo a bright color
explanation: Regulations require shippers to put hazard warning labels on packages, provide proper shipping papers, emergency response information, and placards to communicate the hazard.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: What must a driver do to obtain a hazardous materials endorsement on a CDL?
choice_a: Complete a college chemistry course
choice_b: Pass a written test about transporting hazardous materials
choice_c: Drive a placarded vehicle for six months under supervision
choice_d: Obtain written permission from the shipper
explanation: The manual states that to get a hazardous materials endorsement on a CDL, a driver must pass a written test about transporting hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: What can result from taking shortcuts and breaking hazardous materials rules?
choice_a: A warning letter only
choice_b: Fines and jail
choice_c: A temporary license suspension only for the shipper
choice_d: No consequence if no accident occurs
explanation: The manual warns that non-compliance with hazardous materials regulations can result in fines and jail.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: When a law enforcement officer stops a hazardous materials shipment, what may they check?
choice_a: Only the driver's medical certificate
choice_b: Shipping papers, vehicle placards, the hazardous materials endorsement, and the driver's knowledge of hazardous materials
choice_c: Only the weight of the vehicle
choice_d: Only the condition of the tires
explanation: The manual states officers may check shipping papers, vehicle placards, the hazardous materials endorsement on the driver license, and the driver's knowledge of hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: According to Section 9, all drivers transporting hazardous materials must be trained in security risks. What must this training include?
choice_a: How to recognize and respond to possible security threats
choice_b: How to disarm an explosive device
choice_c: How to negotiate with hijackers
choice_d: How to install a vehicle alarm system
explanation: The manual states all drivers must be trained in the security risks of hazardous materials transportation, including how to recognize and respond to possible security threats.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested, according to the regulations described in Section 9?
choice_a: Once, at the start of employment only
choice_b: Every year
choice_c: At least once every three years
choice_d: Every five years
explanation: The manual states the regulations require that hazardous materials employees be trained and tested at least once every three years.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: Which of these is a shipper's responsibility when offering a hazardous material for transportation?
choice_a: Determine the product's identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group
choice_b: Decide the driver's delivery route
choice_c: Fuel the delivery vehicle
choice_d: Perform the vehicle's pre-trip brake inspection
explanation: The shipper uses the hazardous materials regulations to determine the product's identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group, then must package, mark, label, and placard accordingly.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-1

question: Before transportation begins, what must the carrier check?
choice_a: That the shipper correctly described, marked, labeled, and otherwise prepared the shipment
choice_b: That the driver has a college degree
choice_c: That the consignee has paid in advance
choice_d: That the vehicle has a full tank of fuel
explanation: The carrier's duties include checking, prior to transportation, that the shipper correctly described, marked, labeled, and otherwise prepared the shipment, and refusing improper shipments.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: Which of the following is listed as a driver's responsibility for hazardous materials shipments?
choice_a: Refuse leaking packages and shipments
choice_b: Repackage any leaking container found during the trip
choice_c: Determine the shipment's packing group
choice_d: Assign the shipment's identification number
explanation: The driver's responsibilities include making sure the shipper has identified, marked, and labeled materials properly, and refusing leaking packages and shipments.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: How many different hazard classes are there under the hazardous materials regulations?
choice_a: Five
choice_b: Seven
choice_c: Nine
choice_d: Twelve
explanation: The manual states 'There are nine different hazard classes' and lists the types of materials included in each in Figure 9.1.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: What is a shipping paper?
choice_a: A document such as a shipping order, bill of lading, or manifest that describes the hazardous materials being transported
choice_b: The driver's daily log book
choice_c: A receipt given to the consignee only
choice_d: The vehicle's registration certificate
explanation: The manual states 'A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: While driving, where must a driver keep hazardous materials shipping papers?
choice_a: In the glove compartment, locked
choice_b: In a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within immediate reach while the seat belt is fastened
choice_c: In the sleeper berth
choice_d: In the trailer with the cargo
explanation: Drivers must keep hazardous materials shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within immediate reach while the seat belt is fastened while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: What shape are the hazard warning labels shippers put on hazardous materials packages?
choice_a: Round
choice_b: Diamond-shaped
choice_c: Square, flat on the side
choice_d: Triangular
explanation: Shippers put diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on most hazardous materials packages; if the label won't fit, it may be put on a securely attached tag instead.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-2

question: What are placards used for?
choice_a: To identify the hazard class of the cargo to warn others
choice_b: To advertise the carrier's company name
choice_c: To indicate the vehicle's maximum speed
choice_d: To show the driver's route number
explanation: Placards are signs put on the outside of a vehicle and on bulk packages that identify the hazard class of the cargo, warning others of the hazard.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-3

question: How many identical placards must a placarded vehicle display, and where?
choice_a: Two, one on each side only
choice_b: At least four identical placards, on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_c: One on the rear only
choice_d: Three, on the front and both sides only
explanation: A placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides, readable from all four directions.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-3

question: What letters precede a hazardous material's four-digit identification number?
choice_a: HM or PG
choice_b: NA or UN
choice_c: RQ or EX
choice_d: DOT or EPA
explanation: The manual states identification numbers are a four-digit code, and 'The letters "NA" or "UN" will precede the identification number.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-3

question: What does the U.S. DOT's Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) provide?
choice_a: Delivery schedules for hazardous cargo
choice_b: A list of chemicals and the identification numbers assigned to them
choice_c: State permit fee schedules
choice_d: Driver medical certification standards
explanation: The Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) lists the chemicals and the identification numbers assigned to them, and is used by first responders to identify hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-3

question: Before transporting a material, which lists should you check to determine whether it is regulated?
choice_a: Only the shipper's invoice
choice_b: The Hazardous Materials Table, the List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities, and the List of Marine Pollutants
choice_c: Only the vehicle's registration record
choice_d: Only the carrier's insurance policy
explanation: There are three main lists used to identify hazardous materials: Section 172.101 (Hazardous Materials Table), Appendix A (List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities), and Appendix B (List of Marine Pollutants).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-3

question: In the Hazardous Materials Table, what does an entry of "Forbidden" in Column 3 mean?
choice_a: The material may only be shipped by air
choice_b: You must never transport that material
choice_c: The material requires no placard
choice_d: The material may be shipped with a reduced-fee placard
explanation: Column 3 shows a material's hazard class or division, or the entry 'Forbidden.' The manual instructs: 'Never transport a "Forbidden" material.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-4

question: In the Hazardous Materials Table, a "G" symbol in Column 1 means the shipping name is generic. What must accompany a generic shipping name on the shipping paper?
choice_a: The shipper's home address
choice_b: A technical name identifying the specific chemical that makes the product hazardous
choice_c: The driver's CDL number
choice_d: The consignee's phone number
explanation: The (G) symbol means the shipping name is generic and 'must be accompanied by a technical name on the shipping paper,' identifying the specific hazardous chemical.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-4

question: The letters "NA" preceding an identification number indicate what?
choice_a: The shipping name is used only within the United States and to and from Canada
choice_b: The material is not regulated
choice_c: The material is radioactive
choice_d: The shipment requires no shipping paper
explanation: Identification numbers are preceded by the letters 'UN' or 'NA.' The letters 'NA' are associated with proper shipping names that are only used within the United States and to and from Canada.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-4

question: In Column 7 of the Hazardous Materials Table, what does an entry of the numbers 1-6 mean?
choice_a: The hazardous material is a poison inhalation hazard (PIH) with special shipping paper, marking, and placard requirements
choice_b: The material may only be carried in quantities of 1 to 6 pounds
choice_c: The material requires 1 to 6 placards on the vehicle
choice_d: The shipment needs 1 to 6 signatures on the manifest
explanation: The numbers 1-6 in Column 7 mean the hazardous material is a poison inhalation hazard (PIH); PIH materials have special requirements for shipping papers, marking, and placards.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-5

question: When a hazardous substance is being transported in a reportable quantity (RQ) or greater in one package, what must the shipper display?
choice_a: Nothing extra beyond the normal label
choice_b: The letters RQ on the shipping paper and the package
choice_c: A red flag on the vehicle
choice_d: A special DOT permit number only
explanation: When materials are transported in a reportable quantity or greater in one package, the shipper displays the letters RQ on the shipping paper and package.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-5

question: If the words INHALATION HAZARD appear on the shipping paper or package, what must the driver display?
choice_a: Nothing additional; the hazard class placard alone is sufficient
choice_b: POISON INHALATION HAZARD or POISON GAS placards in addition to any other placards required by the product's hazard class
choice_c: A yellow caution flag only
choice_d: A CORROSIVE placard instead of the normal placard
explanation: If INHALATION HAZARD appears, the rules require display of the POISON INHALATION HAZARD or POISON GAS placards, in addition to other placards required by the product's hazard class, even for small amounts.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-5

question: What marking must bulk packages of a Marine Pollutant display?
choice_a: A red circle with a slash
choice_b: A white triangle with a fish and an "X" through the fish
choice_c: A blue diamond with an anchor
choice_d: A green square with a wave symbol
explanation: Any bulk packages of a Marine Pollutant must display the Marine Pollutant marking, a white triangle with a fish and an 'X' through the fish, on the outside of the vehicle, plus a shipping paper notation.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-5

question: If a hazardous materials shipping paper has more than one page, what must the first page show?
choice_a: The driver's signature only
choice_b: The total number of pages, for example "Page 1 of 4"
choice_c: The vehicle's odometer reading
choice_d: The date the vehicle was last inspected
explanation: A shipping paper with more than one page must have the first page tell the total number of pages, for example, 'Page 1 of 4.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-5

question: On a hazardous materials shipping paper, what is the correct order for the basic description?
choice_a: Packing group, hazard class, identification number, proper shipping name
choice_b: Identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, and packing group
choice_c: Proper shipping name, driver's name, packing group, identification number
choice_d: Hazard class, packing group, identification number, proper shipping name
explanation: The basic description of hazardous materials includes the identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, and the packing group, if any, in that order.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-6

question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous products, how must the hazardous materials be identified?
choice_a: Entered first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or identified by an "X" or "RQ" in the "HM" column
choice_b: Listed only on a separate attached sheet
choice_c: Written in the smallest font on the page
choice_d: Marked with a checkmark next to the driver's signature
explanation: Hazardous materials on a mixed shipping paper must be entered first, highlighted in a contrasting color, OR identified by an 'X' (or 'RQ' for a reportable quantity) placed before the shipping description in a column captioned 'HM.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-6

question: Who is responsible for the emergency response telephone number that must appear on hazardous materials shipping papers?
choice_a: The driver
choice_b: The shipper
choice_c: The consignee
choice_d: The state highway patrol
explanation: Shipping papers must list an emergency response telephone number (unless excepted), and 'the emergency response telephone number is the responsibility of the shipper.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-6

question: When is a shipper's certification on the shipping paper NOT required?
choice_a: Never; it is always required
choice_b: When the shipper is a private carrier transporting their own product, or the package is provided by the carrier (such as a cargo tank)
choice_c: When the shipment weighs less than 100 pounds
choice_d: When the driver has a hazmat endorsement
explanation: The only exceptions to the shipper's certification requirement are when the shipper is a private carrier transporting its own product and when the package is provided by the carrier, such as a cargo tank.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-8

question: Which of the following must a shipper print on a hazardous materials package, when required?
choice_a: The name and address of shipper or consignee, the material's shipping name and identification number, and required labels
choice_b: The carrier's DOT number only
choice_c: The driver's name and CDL number
choice_d: The vehicle's license plate number
explanation: When required, the shipper must put the name and address of shipper or consignee, the hazardous material's shipping name and identification number, and the required labels on the package.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-8

question: When transporting hazardous wastes, what must a driver sign and carry?
choice_a: A Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, signed by hand
choice_b: A verbal agreement recorded on tape
choice_c: A copy of the consignee's business license
choice_d: A blank shipping paper to fill in upon delivery
explanation: When transporting hazardous wastes, you must sign by hand and carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest; treat the manifest as a shipping paper for the waste.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-8

question: When are you allowed to move an improperly placarded vehicle?
choice_a: Only during an emergency, to protect life or property
choice_b: Any time, as long as it is a short distance
choice_c: Only at night
choice_d: Only with police escort
explanation: You must attach the appropriate placards before driving; you are only allowed to move an improperly placarded vehicle during an emergency, in order to protect life or property.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-8

question: Which of these is a requirement for how placards must be displayed on a vehicle?
choice_a: Each placard must be at least three inches away from any other markings
choice_b: Placards may overlap ladders or tarpaulins if space is limited
choice_c: The word "CAUTION" must be printed above every placard
choice_d: Placards may be angled sideways if space is tight
explanation: Placards must be kept at least three inches away from any other markings, easily seen, level, clear of attachments, and affixed to a background of contrasting color; slogans are prohibited on placards.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-8

question: What is the difference between Table 1 and Table 2 hazard classes for placarding purposes?
choice_a: Table 1 materials must be placarded in any amount; Table 2 materials (except bulk packaging) need placards only at 1,001 pounds or more
choice_b: Table 1 applies only to liquids, Table 2 only to solids
choice_c: Table 2 materials never require placards
choice_d: Table 1 applies only to rail transport
explanation: Table 1 materials must be placarded whenever any amount is transported. Table 2 hazard classes, except for bulk packaging, need placards only if the total amount transported is 1,001 pounds or more.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-9

question: When may a driver use a single DANGEROUS placard instead of separate placards for each Table 2 hazard class?
choice_a: When no more than 2,205 pounds of any single Table 2 hazard class material is loaded at any one place
choice_b: Anytime a Table 2 material is on board, with no weight limit
choice_c: Only when hauling explosives
choice_d: Only on tank vehicles
explanation: A DANGEROUS placard may be used instead of separate Table 2 placards only if the driver has not loaded 2,205 pounds or more of any one Table 2 hazard class material at any one place; that material's specific placard must be used above that threshold.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-9

question: What is bulk packaging, for hazmat placarding purposes?
choice_a: Any package weighing more than 50 pounds
choice_b: A single container with a capacity of 119 gallons or more
choice_c: Any package requiring two people to lift
choice_d: Any container used more than once
explanation: Bulk packaging is a single container with a capacity of 119 gallons or more. A bulk package, and the vehicle transporting it, must be placarded even if it only has the residue of a hazardous material.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-9
